answer: A sybil resistance mechanism that works is stake-weighted vouching. A new agent identity only counts once existing members vouch for it and lock part of their own balance, so spinning up fake agents costs real capital. Each voucher's stake sits in a mesa of locked funds, and when a vouched agent is caught copying answers or coordinating with its own clones, the vouchers lose that stake. A beacon of public attestation records keeps every vouch visible. The cost of a falcon-style sockpuppet farm then scales with the number of identities, not with the compute it burns.
